To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of Ni to the Sn–Cu solder significantly decreases the thickness of the Cu3Sn layer, and consequently also of the total IMC thickness.

(i) Ag and Fe do not affect the growth kinetics of the Cu6Sn5 IMC, (ii) Ag and Fe decrease the thickness of the Cu3Sn layer, (iii) Au and Ni decrease the total IMC thickness, (iv) Au decreases the Cu3Sn thickness, (v) Ni decreases both Cu6Sn5 thickness and Cu3Sn thickness.
Ni and Au have strong effects on the growth kinetics and morphology of the Cu6Sn5 IMC layer in the Sn–Ag–Cu system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the alloying element on the growth kinetics, the morphology of the IMC layers, the microstructure of the Cu substrate and the solder joint strength.
the effect of alloying elements on the interfacially grown intermetallic compound layer thicknesses and their growth kinetics in the Sn– Cu system.
the influence of Ag, Fe and Ni additions to Sn–Cu system on the growth kinetics and morphology of the intermetallic compounds formed at the interface between Sn-based solder alloys and Cu substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alloying of Sn–Cu system with Ag, Fe or Au does not affect the IMC growth behaviour significantly, whereas Ni has a strong effect on the growth of Cu6Sn 5 and Cu3Sn.
the elements that are dissolved in the Cu6Sn5 phase have stronger effect on its growth kinetics and consequently on the growth kinetics in the Sn– Cu system than those dissolved in the Cu3Sn phase.

the growth kinetics of Cu6Sn 5 is not significantly affected by the alloying elements studied here, whereas the growth kinetics of the Cu3Sn layer is affected by the alloy elements in the following order: Ni > Au > Fe > Ag.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
alloying of Cu substrate with Ni or Au can be used to decrease the IMC layer growth rate, while the alloying with Fe or Ag is not efficient.

the alloying element’s effect on the IMC growth kinetics in the Sn– Cu system is determined by the solubility in the IMC’s and the effect of the alloying element on the growth kinetics is proportional to its concentration in the IMC layer.
Ni and Au are the most effective elements for reducing the thickness of the Sn–Cu IMC layers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of alloying elements on the growth kinetics can be predicted based on their solubility in IMC’s.
alloying elements that are soluble in the IMC’s have stronger effect on their growth kinetics than elements that do not have such a solubility.
the growth kinetics of IMC’s is not only dependent on the solubilities of alloying elements in Sn–Cu IMC’s, but also on the solubibilities of the alloying element in Cu.
